instruction: I need audio feedback for what's on my screen. Could you activate the screen reader so it reads text aloud?

command: import pyautogui; import time; pyautogui.click({SCREEN_WIDTH_HALF}, {SCREEN_HEIGHT_HALF}); time.sleep(0.5);

result.command: SCREEN_READER=$(timeout 10 gsettings get org.gnome.desktop.a11y.applications screen-reader-enabled 2>/dev/null); if [ "$SCREEN_READER" = "true" ]; then echo "Screen reader enabled"; else echo "Screen reader not enabled"; fi

metadata.explanation: Task requires enabling the screen reader (Orca) for audio feedback. The evaluator checks if org.gnome.desktop.a11y.applications screen-reader-enabled is set to true via gsettings.
metadata.verification: Verified that gsettings command checks screen-reader-enabled boolean value in org.gnome.desktop.a11y.applications schema

Include/exclude patterns are semantically correct: includes 'Screen reader enabled', excludes 'Screen reader not enabled' and 'error'
Coverage is complete: instruction asks to activate screen reader, evaluator verifies it's enabled
